mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about average power?

options.A: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken.
options.B: Average power is the same as instantaneous power at every instant during the motion.
options.C: Average power can be expressed as the product of force and average velocity.
options.D: The SI unit of average power is the watt.

mcqs.answer: Average power is the same as instantaneous power at every instant during the motion.
mcqs.explanation: Average power is defined as the total work done divided by the total time (option A). It is not equal to instantaneous power at each moment; instantaneous power varies with time, while average power is a single overall value. Options C and D are true statements. Hence, option B is the misconception.

mcqs.question: A particle experiences a force of 10 N in the direction of its motion and at a particular instant its speed is 4 m/s. What is the instantaneous power delivered to the particle at that instant?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power P = F·v when force and velocity are collinear. Here P = 10 N × 4 m/s = 40 J/s = 40 W. The other options result from incorrect arithmetic or using wrong formulas.

mcqs.question: Two machines lift loads vertically. Machine A lifts a 200 kg load through 5 m in 2 s. Machine B lifts a 100 kg load through 10 m in 1 s. Which machine has the greater average power output?

options.C: Both have the same average power
options.D: It cannot be determined without the value of g

mcqs.explanation: Work = m·g·h (take g = 10 m/s²). Machine A: W = 200×10×5 = 10,000 J, power = 10,000/2 = 5,000 W. Machine B: W = 100×10×10 = 10,000 J, power = 10,000/1 = 10,000 W. Machine B delivers twice the average power of Machine A. Option D is unnecessary because g cancels when comparing equal‑height work values.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A car of mass 800 kg moves with a constant speed of 20 m/s on a horizontal road. The engine provides a constant tractive force that exactly balances a resistive force of 400 N. What is the power delivered by the engine?
mcqs.explanation: When speed is constant, engine force equals resistive force (400 N). Power = force × velocity = 400 N × 20 m/s = 8,000 W = 8 kW. Options A, C, D correspond to incorrect multiplication or unit conversion.

mcqs.question: Average power is defined as:
mcqs.explanation: Average power = total work (or energy) transferred divided by the total time taken. Options B, C, and D describe different physical quantities (work, specific energy, and force respectively).

mcqs.question: Instantaneous power at a given moment is best described as:

options.A: The derivative of work with respect to time
options.B: Total work done divided by total time

mcqs.answer: The derivative of work with respect to time
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power P(t) = dW/dt. It represents how fast work is being done at that exact instant. Option B describes average power, while C and D are unrelated.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes power from work?

options.A: Work is energy transferred, while power is the rate at which work is done.
options.B: Work is measured in watts, whereas power is measured in joules.
options.C: Work depends on time, but power does not.
options.D: Work is a vector quantity, whereas power is a scalar.

mcqs.answer: Work is energy transferred, while power is the rate at which work is done.
mcqs.explanation: Work (J) is the amount of energy transferred. Power (W) quantifies how quickly that work is performed (J/s). Option B swaps the units, C reverses the dependence on time, and D incorrectly labels work as a vector (work is scalar).

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A 50 N horizontal force acts on a crate that moves at a constant speed of 3 m/s. What is the power delivered to the crate?
mcqs.explanation: Power = force × velocity = 50 N × 3 m/s = 150 J/s = 150 W. Options B and C arise from misplaced decimal points, and D is too large.
